overview: Cardinham Woods is a big Forestry England woodland just outside Bodmin, with trails through the trees, a café and a car park. It’s a great change of scene from the coast, and a lifesaver on a blustery day when the beaches are too wild.
It’s a favourite with dog owners, with trails to explore and even a dog wash for muddy paws on the way home.

expect.title: Woodland trails
expect.text: Trails lead off through the forest from the car park, and the Ranger’s Hut has information and activity packs for children.

expect.title: Café
expect.text: The Woods Café is open every day, so it’s easy to build a walk around a cuppa.

expect.title: Dog-friendly
expect.text: There’s a card-operated dog wash by the car park for after your walk.

goodToKnow.label: Opening
goodToKnow.text: The car park and trails are open from 6am to 9pm every day.

goodToKnow.label: Parking
goodToKnow.text: Parking is paid and goes towards looking after the forest. Members park free.

goodToKnow.label: Getting there
goodToKnow.text: From Bodmin, head along the A38 towards Liskeard and follow the brown signs just beyond the Carminnow Cross roundabout. The last stretch is a single-track road with passing places.

goodToKnow.label: Without a car
goodToKnow.text: There’s no bus to the woods themselves; the nearest stop is about a 25-minute walk away along the road, with no pavement.

goodToKnow.label: Access
goodToKnow.text: Off-road mobility scooters can be hired from the Ranger’s Hut.

week.text: Cardinham is a handy option for a breezy or showery day when the coast is too wild, or for a leg-stretch on travel day as it’s close to the A30 and A38. Combine it with Bodmin Jail or Lanhydrock for a full inland day.

tips: Bring wellies or walking boots: woodland trails get muddy after rain.
Check the café’s own website for its opening hours.
